added: Experimental: turn on Suggest the next dance in Settings ▸ Experimental ▸ Suggestions to add Suggested to the Sort menu of the program builder's dance list. It orders the dances for the end of the program by variety on the matrix, formation balance, the difficulty curve and recent calls at the program's venue, and each dance says why, with Why? listing every reason. It is off by default, and the list still opens in your usual order.

What suggestions look for, in the same section, sets how much each of those counts (Off, A little or A lot), the shape of the difficulty curve and how far back recent calls go, with Reset to defaults.
English dances aren't covered by suggestions yet: they are listed after the others and say so.
A dance already in the program stays in the Suggested list but goes to the bottom, marked Already in this program.
Both Suggestions settings are in your backup, and sync to your other devices once every device in the store has a version of the app that knows them.
changed: In the program builder's add-dance list (not Replace dance), the Called and Not called filters and the Last called sort no longer count the program you are building as calling history.

added: Add rankSuggestions, SuggestionRequest and SuggestionRanking, a pure-Dart scorer for the next dance of a program, and SuggestionSettings with readSuggestionSettings and isValidStoredSuggestionSettings for the stored suggestion_settings value.
Add buildMatrixRow, matrixColumnForKey, ProgramMatrix.isCollisionOnMove and ProgramMatrix.neighborRowIndices.
Add ProgramRepository.latestCallByDance, the newest call per dance under a CalledFilter.
Add SuggestionCandidate, the part of a dance the scorer reads, and SuggestionWorker, a long-lived isolate that ranks and keeps the candidates it was sent.
DanceRepository.search takes currentProgramId, which leaves that program's slots out of the Last called sort as a CalledFilter's currentProgramId does.
Add the suggestions.v1 sync capability, gating suggestions_enabled and suggestion_settings, and classify both keys in the settings privacy registry.
